questions.q: If the time period is doubled, then the angular momentum of the body will (provided the moment of inertia of the body is constant)
questions.solution:
As we know.

$L = I\omega$

$⇒ L = I \times \dfrac{2\pi}{T}$

$L ∝ \dfrac{1}{T}$

Given, ${T}_{2} = 2T$

Hence~$\dfrac{L1}{L2} = \dfrac{2T}{T}$

$⇒ {L}_{2} = \dfrac{L1}{2}$

questions.solution: We know that K=$\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{l} \omega^{2}$where $K=$ kinetic energy $\begin{array}{l}$I=$\text { moment of inertia }$\\ $\omega=\text { angular speed } \end{array}$So, $\quad \omega \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{I}}\begin{aligned} \omega_{1}$: \omega_{2}: \omega_{3} &=$\frac{1}{\sqrt{I_{1}}}$: $\frac{1}{\sqrt{I_{2}}}$: $\frac{1}{\sqrt{I_{3}}}$\\ &=$\frac{1}{\sqrt{1}}$: $\frac{1}{\sqrt{1}}$: $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\sqrt{2}$: $\sqrt{2}$: 1 \end{aligned}

questions.q: A thin circular ring of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is rotating in a horizontal plane about an axis vertical to its plane with a constant angular velocity $\omega$. If two objects each of mass $m$ be attached gently to the opposite ends of a diameter of the ring, the ring will then rotate with an angular velocity
questions.solution: Key Idea Apply law of conservation of angular momentum. $\mathrm{I}_1 \omega_1=\mathrm{I}_2 \omega_2$ In the given case $\begin{aligned} \mathrm{I}_1 & =\mathrm{MR}^2 \\ \mathrm{I}_2 & =\mathrm{MR}^2+2 \mathrm{mR}^2 \\ \omega_1 & =\omega \end{aligned}$ Then $\omega_2=\frac{I_1}{I_2} \omega=\frac{M}{M+2 m} \omega$

questions.q: The ratio of the accelerations for a solid sphere (mass 'm' and radius 'R') rolling down an incline of angle ' $\theta$ ' without slipping and slipping down the incline without rolling is:
questions.solution:
For solid sphere rolling without slipping on inclined plane, acceleration a_{1}=$\frac{g \sin \theta}{1+\frac{K^{2}}{R^{2}}}$For solid sphere slipping on inclined plane without rolling, acceleration a_{2}=g \sin $\theta$Therefore required ratio $=\frac{\mathrm{a}_{1}}{\mathrm{a}_{2}}$
=$\frac{1}{1+\frac{K^{2}}{R^{2}}}=\frac{1}{1+\frac{2}{5}}=\frac{5}{7}$

questions.q: Two rings of radius $\mathrm{R}$ and $\mathrm{nR}$ made of same material have the ratio of moment of inertia about an axis passing through centre is 1: 8 . The value of $\mathrm{n}$ is
questions.solution:
Ratio of moment of inertia of the rings
$\frac{\mathrm{I}_{1}}{\mathrm{I}_{2}}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{M}_{1}}{\mathrm{M}_{2}}\right)\left(\frac{\mathrm{R}_{1}}{\mathrm{R}_{2}}\right)^{2}$
$\begin{aligned}=&\left(\frac{\lambda l_{1}}{\lambda l_{2}}\right)\left(\frac{R_{1}}{R_{2}}\right)^{2}=\left(\frac{2 \pi \mathrm{R}}{2 \pi \mathrm{n} \mathrm{R}}\right)\left(\frac{\mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{n} \mathrm{R}}\right)^{2} \\ &(\lambda=\text { linear density of wire }=\mathrm{constant}) \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\mathrm{I}_{1}}{\mathrm{I}_{2}}=\frac{1}{\mathrmn^{3}}=\frac{1}{8} \quad \text { (given) } \\ \therefore \quad \mathrmn^{3}=8 \Rightarrow \mathrm{n}=2 \end{aligned}$

questions.q: A uniform solid spherical ball is rolling down a smooth inclined plane from a height $h$. The velocity attained by the ball when it reaches the bottom of the inclined plane is v. If the ball is now thrown vertically upwards with the same velocity $v$, the maximum height to which the ball will rise is
questions.solution: We know that total kinetic energy of a body rolling without slipping $K_{\text {total }}=K_{\text {rot }}+K_{\text {trans }}$ For solid spherical ball, $I=\frac{2}{5} m R^{2}$ (along to diameter) and $v=R \omega$ where $R$ is radius of spherical ball So. K_{\text {total }}=\frac{1}{2}\$left(\frac{2}{5}$m R^{2}\right) \$omega^{2}+\frac{1}{2}$m R^{2} \omega^{2} $\begin{array}{l} =\frac{7}{10}$m R^{2} \omega^{2} \\ $K=\frac{7}{10}$m v^{2} \end{array} Potential energy = Kinetic energy $\begin{aligned}$m g h &$=\frac{7}{10}$m v^{2} \\ v^{2} &$=\frac{10}{7}$g h \end{aligned} For vertical projection, $\begin{array}{c}$v^{2}=u^{2}+2 g h^{\prime} \\ $\frac{10}{7}$g h=0+2 g h^{\prime} \Rightarrow h^{\$prime}=\frac{5}{7} h \end{array}

questions.q: A chain of mass $m$ forming a circle of radius $\text{R}$ is slipped on a smooth round cone with half-angle $\text{\theta}$. Find the tension in the chain if it rotates with a constant angular velocity $\text{\omega}$ about a vertical axis coinciding with the symmetry axis of the cone.
questions.solution:
Every element of chain moves on a circular path. So, every element of the chain experiences centripetal force. We consider a small element $\Delta\text{m}$ on the chain making angle $\text{\Delta \theta}$ at the centre





$\text{\Delta N sin \theta = \Delta mg}$...... (i)

Net force towards centre is

$2 \text{T} \text\sin \dfrac{\Delta \theta}{2} - \Delta \text{N} \text\cos \theta = \Delta \text{mR} {ω}^{2}$

$\Delta N ⁡ \text\cos \theta = 2 T ⁡ \text\sin \dfrac{\Delta \theta}{2} - \Delta \text{mR} {ω}^{2}$.......... (ii)

From eqn.(i) and (ii) we get

$\text\cos \theta = \dfrac{2 \text{T} \text\sin \dfrac{\Delta \theta}{2} - \Delta \text{mR} {ω}^{2}}{\Delta \text{mg}}$

But $\text{\Delta \theta}$ is very small.

∴ $\text\sin \dfrac{\Delta \theta}{2} = \dfrac{\Delta \theta}{2}$

∵ $\text\cot \theta = \dfrac{\text{T} \Delta \theta - \Delta \text{mR} {ω}^{2}}{\Delta \text{mg}}$

Here Δm makes an angle Δθ at the centre. The total mass of chain is m.

∴ The mass of chain per unit angle is

$\lambda = \dfrac{m ⁡}{2 \pi}$

∴ $\Delta m ⁡ = \lambda \Delta \theta = \dfrac{m ⁡}{2 \pi} \Delta \theta = \dfrac{m ⁡ \Delta \theta}{2 \pi}$

∴ $\text\cot\theta = \dfrac{\text{T}\Delta\theta - \left(\dfrac{m\Delta\theta}{2\pi}\right)R{ω}^{2}}{\left(\dfrac{m}{2\pi} \Delta\theta\right)g}$

∴ $T ⁡ = \left(R ⁡ {ω}^{2} + \text{g} \text\cot \theta\right) \dfrac{m ⁡}{2 \pi}$
questions.source: Highly selective Backlog Qs for JEE Main

questions.q: The moment of inertia of a rigid body in terms of its angular momentum $L$ and kinetic energy $K$ is
questions.solution:
Angular momentum of a rigid body about a fixed axis is given by

$L = I\omega$

Where $I$ is moment of inertia and $\omega$ is angular velocity about that axis.

Kinetic energy of body is given by

$K = \dfrac{1}{2}I{\omega}^{2}$

$∴K = \dfrac{1}{2I}{\left(I\omega\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{L^{2}}{2I}$

$⇒I = \dfrac{L^{2}}{2K}$
questions.source: Highly selective Backlog Qs for JEE Main

questions.q: Two discs of same moment of inertia $( I )$ are rotating in same sense about their regular axis passing through centre and perpendicular to the plane of disc with angular velocities ${\omega}_{1}$ and ${\omega}_{2}$. They are brought into contact face to face coinciding the axis of rotation. The expression for loss in energy during this process is
questions.solution:
The initial angular momentum of two discs is ${I}_{1}{ω}_{1} + {I}_{2}{ω}_{2} = I \left({ω}_{1} + {ω}_{2}\right).

The final angular momentum of system is \left({I}_{1} + {I}_{2}\right)\omega =$2I$\omega

From the conservation of angular momentum, \omega = \dfrac{{ω}_{1} + {ω}_{2}}{2}.

Initial kinetic energy, $K{E}_{i} = $\dfrac{1}{2}$I \left({ω}_{1}^{2} + {ω}_{2}^{2}\right)$

and final kinetic energy, $K{E}_{f} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(2I\right)\dfrac{\left({ω}_{1} + {ω}_{2}\right)2}{4}$

Loss in kinetic energy is $\Delta KE = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{{I}_{1}{I}_{2}}{{I}_{1} + {I}_{2}}{\left({\omega}_{1} - {\omega}_{2}\right)}^{2}$
$= \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{I^{2}}{\left(2I\right)}{\left({\omega}_{1} - {\omega}_{2}\right)}^{2}$
$= \dfrac{1}{4}I{\left({\omega}_{1} - {\omega}_{2}\right)}^{2}$

$

questions.q: The $y –$~coordinate of centre of mass of a thin and uniform semicircular ring of radius $r$ shown in figure is
questions.solution:
The wire is uniform. So, the mass per unit length of the wire& $\mu = \dfrac{M}{\pir}$.

Let us assume a small element on the semicircular ring as shown in the figure.

Mass of the element~$dm = \left(\dfrac{M}{\pir}\right)\left(rd\theta\right) = \dfrac{M}{π}d\theta$

The~$y$-coordinate of the centre of mass

${y}_{cm} = \dfrac{1}{M} ∫ ydm ⇒ {y}_{cm} = \dfrac{1}{M}{∫}_{0}^{π}\left(rsin\theta\right)\left(\dfrac{M}{π}\right)d\theta ⇒ {y}_{cm} = \dfrac{r}{π}\left[1 + 1\right] ⇒ {y}_{cm} = \dfrac{2r}{π}$

questions.q: Two masses are attached to a rod end to end. If torque is applied they rotate with angular acceleration $\alpha$. If their distances are doubled and same torque is applied, then they move with angular acceleration
questions.solution: Suppose the masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ are attached to the ends of a massless rod. $C_1$ is the axis of rotation which is at a distance $R$ from each of the masses. $\therefore$ the moment of inertia of the system, $\mathrm{I}=$m_1 R²+m_2 R²=\left($m_1+m_2\right) R² Now if the distance between the masses is doubled, then the moment of inertia \Gamma=m_1(2 R)^2+m_2(2 R)^2=\left($m_1+m_2\right) 4 R² Since the same torque is applied in both the cases, $\begin{aligned}$& \tau=I $\alpha=$I^{\prime} $\alpha^{\prime}$\\ & \Rightarrow $\alpha^{\prime}=\frac{I \alpha}{I^{\prime}}=\frac{\left(m_1+m_2\right) R^2 \alpha}{\left(m_1+m_2\right) 4 R^2}=\frac{\alpha}{4} \end{aligned}$
questions.source: Highly selective Backlog Qs for JEE Main
